note: Burn transitive; initial stress. Contrasts with intransitive daažis by consonant, both root-stressed.
Come; unmarked short citation.
Cry; unmarked, central/rounded u approximate.
Die; final syllable stress.
Drink; unmarked short citation.
Eat; unmarked short citation.
Fly; same form as stand, final stress; possible rise/fly semantic polysemy.
Give; unmarked short citation, homonymous with one day noun but etymologically distinct.
Go; long vowel/sequence, unmarked.
Harvest; printed initial l is a consonant, not an apostrophe. DB 'ɨɨs loses l and creates spurious stress; a lav/lū reap root comparison becomes possible.
Hear; ear plus do, unmarked phrase.
Kill; final stress, unlike root-stressed long-aa burn/laugh/say verbs.
Know; short rounded/central u normalized, not stored ẓaš. No stress mark.
Laugh; initial stress.
Lie down; identical rounded/central u word to sleep193, unmarked; stored šus/sas distinction is not reliable.
Say; initial stress.
See; unmarked short citation.
Sit; unmarked long central vowel.
Sleep; same printed form as lie down189, unmarked.
Stand; final stress, same form as fly181.
Swim; final stress, tentatively Purik loan in source.
Walk; final stress despite long aa in the root, unlike laugh/say. Printed onset z appears plain, not stored retroflex ẓ.
Wash transitive; unmarked rounded/central u.
All singular; unmarked Purik loan.
All plural; same as198, not a separate lexical confirmation.
Big; initial stress; etymology not automatically that of neighboring baṛo.
Bitter; both inherited-looking c̣ito and source-identified Kashmiri tiito are actually in Brokskat. Both initially stressed; keep loan alternative separate.
Black; initial stress, y may be glide before o rather than independent syllable.
Blind; final stress, Purik loan.
Cold; initial stress on doubled y vowel before a; exact syllabification needs source interpretation.
Dry; initial stress, short root, final o.
Eight; unmarked short monosyllable.
Eighteen; final stress, nasalized vowel as printed; exact doubling unclear and not inferred for stress analysis.
Eleven; initial stress.
Few; apo initially stressed. The kʲii alternative has superscript j PALATALIZATION, not a pre-vowel stress apostrophe. Earlier note reading k'ii was mistaken; no stress is printed on kii.
Fifteen; initial stress and nasal long aa.
Five; nasal long oo plus š, no d or s sequence. Stored pods is erroneous.
Forty-one; two-word arithmetic expression with two stresses.
Four; unmarked long vowel.
Fourteen; initial stress.
Full; two alternatives, initial stress on punjis and final stress on peree. Do not merge them into one multiple-accent word or one formation.
Good; initial stress.
Green; initial stress, long ii.
Hot; INITIAL SYLLABLE stress. No acute/mora mark in Brokskat; the stored taáto is a false Brokskat late-mora datum.
Hundred; short unmarked.
Hungry; two comma-separated alternatives, not the DB's combined phrase. Second final-stressed; first unmarked long monosyllable.
Left; palatalized h, not stored b; no stress marked. Purik loan.
Long; initial syllable stress, no acute/mora notation.
Many; initial stress.
New; unmarked long y vowel.
Nine; nasalized long barred/central u, no r. Same normalized vowel spelling as name48; no stress marked.
Nineteen; initial stress despite long final aa. Comparable kunii forms in all Shina columns suggest an inherited subtractive numeral branch; old eka/ūna compound requires checking.
Old person; initial stress.
One; unmarked short vowel.
Red; initial stress; medial consonant is eth-like ð, not necessarily a d stop. This supports a fricative/contraction comparison with lōhila but does not determine mora.
